nodes.label: BasicPoly.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: BasicPoly is a **minimal, portable polynomial value type** the engine uses where the full machinery of Polynomial or gbvector (file-gbring.md) would be overkill — typically for serialisation, test inputs, and the streaming constructors of newer GB code.

nodes.label: BasicPolyList.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: BasicPolyList is a **plain-data polynomial list** — a std::vector<BasicPoly> — used as the **transport format** between M2-side polynomial representations, the F4 GB engine, and serialised file formats. It deliberately *doesn't* require a ring.

nodes.label: BasicPolyListParser.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: BasicPolyListParser.hpp declares parsers that read polynomial data from text (file or string) into the engine's portable BasicPolyList type. Two formats are supported: the engine's own simple text format and **Msolve's** input format.

nodes.label: Eschreyer.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: Eschreyer.cpp implements an **older Schreyer-style resolution** — specifically, a GBKernelComputation that computes the kernel of a matrix between free modules using a Schreyer order on the source. It is the direct predecessor of the newer F4-based implementation in schreyer-resolution/.

nodes.label: ExponentList.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: ExponentList is the newer **sparse exponent-list** encoding for monomials at the top level of the engine. A monomial is stored as a sequence of (variable, exponent) pairs — compact for monomials of low support, easy to iterate without unpacking.

nodes.label: ExponentVector.{hpp}
nodes.summary: ExponentVector is the engine's **dense exponent-vector encoding** for monomials: a fixed-length array of Exponents indexed by variable position. It complements ExponentList, the sparse encoding.

nodes.label: GF.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: GF.hpp declares the **legacy GF** — the engine's original Galois-field class before the aring refactor. It is still constructed by some M2 paths but new code prefers the FLINT-backed file-aring-gf-flint.md and file-aring-gf-flint-big.md or the portable file-aring-m2-gf.md.

nodes.label: LLL.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: LLL.cpp implements the classical **LLL algorithm** for reducing an integer lattice basis. Given a matrix over ZZ whose columns span a lattice, it returns a new basis of the same lattice whose vectors are short and nearly orthogonal.

nodes.label: M2FreeAlgebra.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: M2FreeAlgebra.cpp is the **Ring-shaped wrapper** that lets a non-commutative FreeAlgebra appear to the rest of the engine as just another Ring. The non-commutative implementation lives in NCAlgebras/; this file is the M2-side façade.

nodes.label: M2FreeAlgebraQuotient.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: M2FreeAlgebraQuotient is the **Ring-shaped façade** around a non-commutative quotient algebra. It packages a NCAlgebras/FreeAlgebraQuotient in a Ring subclass so the rest of the engine can treat the quotient like any other ring.

nodes.label: MemoryBlock.{hpp}
nodes.summary: MemoryBlock is the engine's **bump-pointer allocator**, used in the inner loops of F4, the resolution code, and the GB engines whenever a large number of transient small objects need to be allocated and freed together.

nodes.label: NAG.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: NAG.cpp is the engine entry point for **Numerical Algebraic Geometry** — homotopy continuation, witness sets, monodromy, and the other techniques used to numerically describe the zero set of a polynomial system. Originally contributed by Anton Leykin; large portions of the code are in the public domain (see the copyright notice).

nodes.label: Polynomial.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: Polynomial.hpp declares **Monom** and **Poly** — a modern, lightweight polynomial value type shared between the non-commutative algebra code and the newer commutative GB code in gb-f4/. It coexists with the legacy gbvector used by the older GB engines (file-gbring.md).

nodes.label: PolynomialStream.{hpp}
nodes.summary: PolynomialStream.hpp defines a **C++ concept (informally)** that streaming polynomial-input consumers in the refactored F4 path implement. It declares the integer type aliases shared with gb-f4/file-MonomialTypes.md and sketches the protocol an SLP-style streaming producer should follow.

nodes.label: SLP-defs.{hpp}
nodes.summary: SLP-defs.hpp declares the **straight-line program** type hierarchy used by Numerical Algebraic Geometry: SLProgram (the underlying program), M2SLProgram (the M2-facing wrapper), and the opaque type tags they expose. The implementations live in file-SLP.md and SLP-imp.hpp (file-SLP-imp.md).

nodes.label: SLP-imp.{hpp}
nodes.summary: SLP-imp.hpp defines **SLEvaluatorConcrete<RT>** — the templated implementation that evaluates a SLProgram at specific input values. The template is parameterised on the coefficient ring RT so the inner evaluation loop inlines per ring.

nodes.label: SLP.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: A **straight-line program (SLP)** is a directed acyclic graph whose nodes are arithmetic operations on a fixed set of inputs and constants. SLPs are the evaluation model used by Numerical Algebraic Geometry: given a polynomial system once, compile it to an SLP, then evaluate the SLP at every continuation step.

nodes.label: VectorArithmetic.{hpp}
nodes.summary: VectorArithmetic.hpp is the engine's **abstract arithmetic dispatcher** used by the F4 and resolution code paths. It hides the choice of coefficient ring behind a uniform interface so a single algorithm implementation can run against any aring-backed ring.

nodes.label: ZZ.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: ZZ.hpp declares the **legacy Ring-based ZZ** — the engine's original integer ring class, before the aring framework. It is still constructed by some M2 paths but new code prefers file-aring-zz-flint.md.

nodes.label: ZZp.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: ZZp.hpp declares the **legacy Z_mod** — the engine's original Z/p class before the aring framework. It is still in some M2 paths but new code prefers file-aring-zzp.md, file-aring-zzp-flint.md, or file-aring-zzp-ffpack.md.

nodes.label: aring-CC.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: aring-CC.cpp implements the engine's **machine-precision complex numbers** — a pair of doubles wrapped in a SimpleARing specialisation. It is the complex sibling of file-aring-RR.md.

nodes.label: aring-CCC.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: aring-CCC.cpp implements **arbitrary-precision complex numbers** as a pair of MPFR floats (mantissa-precision flexible, IEEE 754 rounding). It is the complex sibling of file-aring-RRR.md.

nodes.label: aring-CCi.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: aring-CCi.cpp implements **complex intervals** — typically represented as a pair of real intervals (one for real part, one for imaginary), or as a rectangle in the complex plane. It is the complex sibling of file-aring-RRi.md.

nodes.label: aring-RR.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: aring-RR.cpp implements the engine's **machine-precision real numbers** — RR backed by hardware double. It is the simplest of the real-number rings, used when speed dominates and precision doesn't need to exceed IEEE 754 double precision.

nodes.label: aring-RRR.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: aring-RRR.cpp implements **arbitrary-precision real numbers** using MPFR's mpfr_t value type. It is the precision-flexible sibling of file-aring-RR.md, used whenever an M2 user specifies a precision other than 53 for RR.

nodes.label: aring-RRi.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: aring-RRi.cpp implements **real intervals** — an interval [a, b] where a, b are MPFR-precision reals and the represented value is "some real in this interval." It uses MPFI (Multiple Precision Floating- point Interval library) for the arithmetic.

nodes.label: aring-gf-flint-big.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: aring-gf-flint-big.cpp implements **Galois fields with arbitrary extension degree** using FLINT's fq_nmod_t value type. Where file-aring-gf-flint.md builds Zech logarithm tables (fast but limited to small q = p^k), this file represents elements as polynomials modulo a primitive polynomial — slower per operation, but no size limit.

nodes.label: aring-gf-flint.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: aring-gf-flint.cpp implements the engine's **Galois field for small extensions** using FLINT's fq_zech_* family — Zech logarithm tables for elements of GF(p^k) where the size is small enough that exhaustive table storage is practical. For large extensions the engine instead uses aring-gf-flint-big.cpp (fq_nmod_*).

nodes.label: aring-glue.{hpp}
nodes.summary: aring-glue.hpp defines the **ConcreteRing<R> template** — the bridge that lets every aring-based coefficient ring appear to the rest of the engine as a legacy Ring*. It is the single most important piece of glue holding the two parallel ring APIs together.

nodes.label: aring-m2-gf.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: aring-m2-gf.cpp implements **Galois fields** entirely in native M2 / engine code without depending on FLINT, Givaro, or any external GF library. It is the **portable fallback** when those libraries are unavailable, and the reference path other GF implementations compare against.

nodes.label: aring-qq-flint.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: aring-qq-flint.cpp implements the engine's **FLINT-backed rationals** using FLINT's fmpq_t value type. It is the modern default QQ implementation; the older aring-qq-gmp.cpp remains available.

nodes.label: aring-qq-gmp.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: ARingQQGMP is the **GMP mpq_t-backed rational ring** — arbitrary-precision rationals through GMP. The legacy ARingQQ wraps this for the Ring interface.

nodes.label: aring-qq.{hpp}
nodes.summary: aring-qq.hpp is a **tiny header** whose only job is to choose a default ARingQQ from among the available QQ implementations and typedef it for the rest of the engine.

nodes.label: aring-tower.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: aring-tower.cpp implements an **iterated tower of finite-field extensions** — used to build very large Galois fields by composition of simpler extensions. It is the engine's general-purpose path for GF(p^k) with large k.

nodes.label: aring-translate.{hpp}
nodes.summary: aring-translate.hpp is the **cross-ring coercion** layer of the aring framework. It declares conversion functions between any two aring-based rings — moving values from Z to Q, Q to RR, Z/p to Z, and so on — at compile-time-resolved speed.

nodes.label: aring-wrap.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: aring-wrap.hpp declares **RElementWrap<RingType>** — a templated wrapper that holds a single aring value (typed by RingType) and exposes it through the abstract RElement interface. It is the type-safe complement of file-aring-glue.md (which wraps a whole *ring*); this file wraps a single *element*.

nodes.label: aring-zz-flint.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: aring-zz-flint.cpp implements the engine's **FLINT-backed Z** — arbitrary-precision integers using FLINT's fmpz_t value type as the storage. It is one of two ZZ implementations alongside the legacy GMP-backed one in aring-zz-gmp.cpp.

nodes.label: aring-zz-gmp.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: aring-zz-gmp.cpp implements **ZZ using GMP's mpz_t** value type directly. It is the original aring ZZ back end; the FLINT-based file-aring-zz-flint.md is now the default because it inlines small-value arithmetic.

nodes.label: aring-zzp-ffpack.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: aring-zzp-ffpack.cpp implements **Z/p** using the FFLAS-FFPACK library's Modular<…> field type. It is the fastest Z/p back end the engine ships for very small primes, especially in matrix-heavy code, because FFLAS-FFPACK ties into BLAS-style dispatch for dense linear algebra.

nodes.label: aring-zzp-flint.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: aring-zzp-flint.cpp implements **Z/p** using FLINT's nmod_t value type. Among the engine's several Z/p back ends, this one is the standard choice for small-to-medium primes when FFLAS-FFPACK is not available or applicable.

nodes.label: aring-zzp.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: aring-zzp.cpp implements **Z/p for small primes** using precomputed log / exp tables of a primitive root. It is the **portable** Z/p back end — no FLINT, no FFLAS-FFPACK dependency, no Givaro.

nodes.label: aring.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: aring.hpp defines the **abstract-ring framework** (namespace M2) that unifies the engine's coefficient rings under one templated interface. Each concrete coefficient ring (ZZ via GMP, ZZ via FLINT, Z/p via FFLAS, GF, RR, CC, …) lives in its own aring-*.{cpp,hpp} pair; this file is the **dispatcher and shared base** that ties them together.

nodes.label: assprime.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: AssociatedPrimes computes the **codimension** and the **associated primes of minimal codimension** of a monomial ideal. It operates on a MonomialIdeal (file-monideal.md) and returns its results in monomial form.

nodes.label: betti.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: BettiDisplay is the engine-side data structure that holds and renders a **Betti table**: the array of ranks β_{i,j} of the *i*-th free module in homological degree *j* of a free resolution.

nodes.label: buffer.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: buffer is the engine's lightweight **append-only byte buffer**. It is used everywhere the engine produces text — pretty-printing, error messages, serialised output, debug traces — as a GC-friendly, leak-proof alternative to std::ostringstream.

nodes.label: coeffrings.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: coeffrings.cpp is the engine's **coefficient-ring registry**: it defines a handful of CoefficientRing<X> classes that wrap concrete arithmetic back ends and register them with the aring framework. The class CoefficientRingZZp declared at the top of the header is the smallest fully-worked example.

nodes.label: comb.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: comb.cpp provides combinatorial helpers used internally by the engine — most notably the Subsets class that enumerates and encodes p-element subsets of {0, 1, …, n-1}.

nodes.label: comp-gb.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: GBComputation is the abstract base for **all** Gröbner basis algorithms in the engine. It subclasses Computation and adds GB-specific entry points (the basis, leading-term matrix, syzygies).

nodes.label: comp-res.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: ResolutionComputation is the abstract base for all **free-resolution** algorithms in the engine, mirroring the role of GBComputation on the GB side. It subclasses Computation and adds resolution-specific methods: per-degree free modules, differentials, Betti tables.

nodes.label: comp.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: comp.hpp and comp.cpp define **Computation** — the abstract base class for **incremental computations** in M2 (Gröbner bases, resolutions, Hilbert series, etc.). The class encapsulates the **stop-condition machinery** that lets users interrupt long-running computations cleanly.

nodes.label: complex.{c,h}
nodes.summary: complex.h declares the engine's **gmp_CC complex number primitives** — initialisation, arithmetic, and special functions on arbitrary-precision complex values built from two MPFR reals.

nodes.label: cra.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: cra.hpp and cra.cpp implement **ChineseRemainder** — the engine's CRT and rational-reconstruction primitives. Used to lift modular computations back to ZZ / QQ.

nodes.label: debug.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: debug.cpp is the engine's **debug-printing toolkit**: a set of d…(…) helper functions, callable from a debugger or from instrumented engine code, that pretty-print engine values to stdout. It is the engine's equivalent of gdb-callable print helpers.

nodes.label: defgroups.{h}
nodes.summary: defgroups.h is **pure Doxygen documentation** — it contains no code. It defines the @ingroup categories that other engine headers use to organise the generated C++ API docs.

nodes.label: det.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: det.cpp implements **determinant** and **minor** computations over the engine's matrix types. It supports three algorithm strategies selectable by the caller.

nodes.label: dmat-ffpack.{cpp}
nodes.summary: dmat-ffpack.cpp is a **legacy / historical file** that was once the FFLAS-FFPACK-routed implementation of DMat<R> linear-algebra operations. The file body is gated under #if 0; the functionality has moved to dmat.cpp and the templated mat-linalg.hpp machinery.

nodes.label: dmat-gf-flint-big.{hpp}
nodes.summary: dmat-gf-flint-big.hpp is a **DMat<M2::ARingGFFlintBig> specialisation** — uses FLINT's fq_nmod_mat_t directly instead of the generic templated path. Faster for matrices over large Galois fields.

nodes.label: dmat-gf-flint.{hpp}
nodes.summary: dmat-gf-flint.hpp and dmat-gf-flint-big.hpp are the **FLINT-backed specialisations** of DMat<R> for Galois-field matrices. The two correspond to FLINT's two GF representations: Zech-log tables for small fields (fq_zech) and polynomial-quotient form for large fields (fq_nmod).

nodes.label: dmat-lu.{hpp}
nodes.summary: The dmat-lu*.hpp family declares **specialised LU decomposition** implementations for the engine's dense matrix type DMat<R>. LU is the workhorse of numerical linear algebra; the specialisations route to back-end-specific code (FLINT, FFLAS-FFPACK, BLAS) when available.

nodes.label: dmat-qq-flint.{hpp}
nodes.summary: dmat-qq-flint.hpp is the **FLINT-backed specialisation** of DMat<R> for QQ matrices. It stores the matrix as a FLINT fmpq_mat_t and dispatches arithmetic to FLINT's rational matrix routines.

nodes.label: dmat-qq-interface-flint.{hpp}
nodes.summary: dmat-qq-interface-flint.hpp is a **bridge layer** that lets the engine perform fast FLINT-matrix arithmetic on a DMat<M2::ARingQQ> (which stores elements as GMP mpq_t values, not FLINT fmpq_t). It translates between the two representations on the way into and out of FLINT calls.

nodes.label: dmat-zz-flint.{hpp}
nodes.summary: dmat-zz-flint.hpp is the **FLINT-backed specialisation** of the engine's DMat<R> template for the ZZ ring. The specialisation stores the matrix as a FLINT fmpz_mat_t and routes arithmetic to FLINT's matrix routines — significantly faster than the generic template path for large integer matrices.

nodes.label: dmat-zzp-flint.{hpp}
nodes.summary: dmat-zzp-flint.hpp is the **FLINT-backed specialisation** of DMat<R> for Z/p (via FLINT's nmod_mat_t). It mirrors file-dmat-zz-flint.md in shape, specialised on the modular-arithmetic FLINT type.

nodes.label: dmat.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: DMat is the engine's **dense-matrix template**, parameterised on a coefficient ring. Specialised instantiations exist for FLINT-backed ZZ, QQ, Z/p, GF, and CC; everything else uses the generic instantiation.

nodes.label: dpoly.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: dpoly.cpp implements **univariate polynomial arithmetic over algebraic extensions of QQ** and over **finite fields**. It supports the GCD and modular GCD operations the engine needs for factorisation, extension construction, and similar tasks.

nodes.label: eigen.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: eigen.cpp implements the engine's **eigenvalue / eigenvector / SVD** routines for real and complex matrices. It is a specialisation of LAPACK (file-lapack.md) plus a fallback path using the Eigen3 C++ template library.

nodes.label: engine-includes.{hpp}
nodes.summary: A 41-line "**umbrella header**" pulled in by every .cpp / .hpp in the engine that needs the standard portability shims. Acts as a **single point of truth** for which platform / config headers to include and in what order — so individual translation units don't have to repeat the dance.

nodes.label: engine.{cpp,h}
nodes.summary: Tiny (≈70-line) translation unit that owns a handful of **engine-wide singletons** that don't have a better home — anything that needs exactly one definition somewhere lives here.

nodes.label: error.{c,h}
nodes.summary: error.c is the engine's **error-reporting primitive**. It maintains a thread-local error message string and provides the macros engine code uses to raise errors that the interpreter surfaces to the M2 user.

nodes.label: exceptions.{hpp}
nodes.summary: exceptions.hpp declares the **C++ exception types** the engine uses internally before they cross the C boundary back to the interpreter. The boundary itself uses the thread-local error string in file-error.md; these exceptions are an intra-engine mechanism for unwinding cleanly through templated code.

nodes.label: finalize.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: finalize.cpp declares the **engine-object finalisation hooks** that let long-lived engine objects (polynomial rings, GBs, monomial ideals, …) be properly torn down when the user releases them. The helpers cooperate with bdwgc to run cleanup code when an object becomes unreachable.

nodes.label: frac.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: FractionField is the engine's representation of the **field of fractions** of an integral domain. Internally it stores fractions as a (numerator, denominator) pair with on-the-fly simplification.

nodes.label: fractionfreeLU.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: fractionfreeLU.cpp implements **fraction-free LU decomposition** of a matrix over an integral domain. It uses the Bareiss algorithm to keep all intermediate computations within the ring — no temporary fractions, even when the base ring is not a field.

nodes.label: franzi-brp.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: These five files implement a **boolean ring polynomial (BRP) GB engine** contributed by Franziska Hinkelmann. Used for fast Gröbner-basis computation in F_2[x_1,...,x_n] / (x_i^2 - x_i) — polynomial rings over F_2 with squares vanishing (the characteristic-2 boolean polynomial ring).

nodes.label: freemod.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: FreeModule is the engine's representation of a free module R^n over a polynomial (or other) ring R. It is the source and target type of every Matrix and the domain/codomain of every map in the resolution code.

nodes.label: gauss.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: gauss.cpp implements an **explicit Gaussian-elimination** computation of a Gröbner basis (or submodule) over a field. It is the engine's straightforward "row-reduce a matrix of generators to echelon form" path — simpler and sometimes faster than the full Buchberger machinery for inputs where the answer really is just linear-algebra reduction.

nodes.label: gb-default.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: gbA is the engine's **default Gröbner basis algorithm** — a Buchberger-style algorithm with carefully chosen S-pair selection, monomial-table reductions, and a tuned gbring value representation. It is the algorithm M2 uses when no Strategy => option overrides the default.

nodes.label: gbring.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: GBRing is a polynomial-ring **view** specialised for Gröbner basis arithmetic. It carries the same data as a PolynomialRing — coefficient ring, monoid, ring flags — but lays out values in a form designed for fast head/tail decomposition, S-pair reduction, and (optionally) implicit Schreyer ordering.

nodes.label: gbweight.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: GBWeight computes the **heuristic weight** of polynomials and monomials during Gröbner basis computation. It is the engine's central source of the "sugar" and degree information that drives S-pair selection.

nodes.label: geobucket.{hpp}
nodes.summary: geobucket.hpp and geopoly.hpp implement **geometric buckets** — the data structure for fast polynomial addition / subtraction used throughout the Gröbner-basis engines and resolutions. The "geo" is geometric (size-doubling buckets).

nodes.label: geopoly.{hpp}
nodes.summary: Defines class polyheap, a **geometric-heap** data structure for adding many polynomials together efficiently. The classic use case is the reduction step in a Gröbner-basis algorithm: you start with one polynomial and add many smaller multiples of basis elements to it, producing a long sum that needs to be combined into a single canonical polynomial.

nodes.label: geovec.{hpp}
nodes.summary: geovec.hpp declares the engine's **geometric heap** specialised for adding many vec values (file-ring-vecs.md) efficiently — the ring-element analogue of gbvectorHeap in file-gbring.md.

nodes.label: godboltTest.{cpp}
nodes.summary: godboltTest.cpp is a **standalone test harness** for verifying log/exp/Zech tables for Z/p over small primes. The file name references Compiler Explorer (popularly "godbolt"), suggesting it was written as a code-style / microbenchmark experiment.

nodes.label: hash.{hpp}
nodes.summary: hash.hpp declares **EngineObject** and **MutableEngineObject** — the two base classes from which essentially every long-lived engine class derives. They provide GC integration, lazy hash computation, and the virtual-destructor anchor every engine subclass shares.

nodes.label: hermite.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: hermite.cpp implements **Hermite normal form** of an integer matrix — the row-equivalent upper-triangular canonical form with positive diagonal and entries above the diagonal smaller than the diagonal entry. For ZZ matrices it plays the role that Gaussian elimination (file-gauss.md) plays over a field.

nodes.label: hilb.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: hilb.cpp implements **Bigatti et al.**'s recursive divide-and-conquer algorithm for computing the Hilbert series of a graded module over a polynomial ring. From the Hilbert series the engine derives the Hilbert function and Hilbert polynomial.

nodes.label: imonorder.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: imonorder.cpp defines the **internal form** of a monomial ordering — the encoded, runtime-friendly representation walked by the inner loop when two monomials are compared. It is the operational counterpart to the declarative MonomialOrdering the user wrote.

nodes.label: int-bag.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: int-bag.hpp declares **int_bag** — a tiny utility class that pairs either a single int (or void*) value with a monomial in varpower form. It is the engine's grab-bag combination of payload + monomial used in scattered places where a (value, monomial) tuple needs to travel together.

nodes.label: interreduce.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: interreduce.cpp defines **Interreducer** — a helper class for performing **inter-reduction** of a list of polynomials. Given a collection of gbvector* values, Interreducer reduces each one modulo the others until no further simplification is possible, producing a Gröbner-basis-like canonical form.

nodes.label: interrupted.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: interrupted.cpp is a **tiny one-function module** exposing the single global predicate system_interrupted() — true iff the user has requested an interrupt (typically by pressing Ctrl+C while M2 was running an engine computation). Every engine inner loop polls this periodically and bails out when it returns true.

nodes.label: lapack.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: lapack.cpp is the engine's **bridge to LAPACK** — the numerical linear-algebra library. It provides linear-equation solving, factorisation, and eigenvalue routines for matrices over RR, CC, RRR, and CCC.

nodes.label: localring.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: LocalRing implements the engine's representation of a **localisation** of a polynomial ring at a prime ideal P. Elements are stored as fractions (numer, denom) where denom is required to lie outside P.

nodes.label: m2tbb.{hpp}
nodes.summary: m2tbb.hpp is the engine's **wrapper around Intel TBB** (Threading Building Blocks) — the parallel-programming primitives the engine uses for F4 inner-loop parallelism and Schreyer-resolution scheduling. The wrapper exists to make TBB an *optional* dependency: when TBB is absent, all the parallel paths compile to no-ops and the engine runs serially.

nodes.label: mat-arith.{hpp}
nodes.summary: mat-arith.hpp declares the **arithmetic operations** for the engine's dense and sparse matrix templates: addition, subtraction, multiplication, scaling, negation. It is the basic-arithmetic counterpart of mat-linalg.hpp.

nodes.label: mat-elem-ops.{hpp}
nodes.summary: mat-elem-ops.hpp defines **elementary matrix operations** — row swap, column swap, row scaling, row reduction by another row — templated on the matrix storage type MT. It supplies the building blocks every linear-algebra algorithm composes.

nodes.label: mat-linalg.{hpp}
nodes.summary: mat-linalg.hpp is the **templated linear-algebra layer** for the engine's dense matrix type DMat<R>. It declares LU, rank, determinant, null-space, solve, inverse — all parameterised on the coefficient ring R.

nodes.label: mat-util.{hpp}
nodes.summary: mat-util.hpp collects **templated helpers** for both DMat<R> and SMat<R> matrices that don't fit naturally under file-mat-arith.md, file-mat-elem-ops.md, or file-mat-linalg.md. The first such helper — displayMat — is the matrix-printing utility used throughout debugging code.

nodes.label: mat.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: mat.hpp and mat.cpp define **MutableMatrix** — the abstract base class for M2's mutable matrices. The dense (DMat) and sparse (SMat if added) implementations inherit from it.

nodes.label: matrix-con.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: MatrixConstructor is the **builder** for the engine's immutable Matrix type. Because Matrix is immutable once constructed, the engine needs a separate, mutable builder that accumulates state and produces a Matrix at the end.

nodes.label: matrix-kbasis.{cpp}
nodes.summary: matrix-kbasis.cpp implements the **k-basis** computation: given a graded module and a set of degrees, return the k-vector-space basis of that module restricted to those degrees. It is the engine code behind M2's basis(d, M) built-in.

nodes.label: matrix-ncbasis.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: matrix-ncbasis.cpp implements the **non-commutative analogue** of file-matrix-kbasis.md's basis(d, M): given a non-commutative algebra module and a degree, enumerate the standard words of that degree.

nodes.label: matrix-sort.{cpp}
nodes.summary: matrix-sort.cpp implements **MatrixSorter** — a helper class that sorts the columns of a Matrix by their leading term, leading degree, or another configurable key. It is the engine code behind M2's sort(M) and mingens(M).

nodes.label: matrix-stream.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: matrix-stream.cpp implements the engine's **streaming matrix construction** API — a builder pattern that accepts polynomials term by term and produces a Matrix at the end. It is the preferred path for reading matrices from text or binary input formats because it never holds the full input in memory.

nodes.label: matrix-symm.{cpp}
nodes.summary: matrix-symm.cpp implements the **symmetric power** of a matrix — the p-th symmetric power Sym^p(M) viewed as a matrix in its own right. For a one-row matrix M = [m_1, …, m_n] of degree-1 entries, Sym^p(M) is the row of all products of p factors taken from M's columns.

nodes.label: matrix.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: Matrix is the engine's representation of a homomorphism F → G between two free modules, where each column of the matrix is a vector in the target free module. It is immutable: every operation that "modifies" a matrix actually returns a new one.

nodes.label: mem.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: mem.cpp implements the engine's **size-class slab allocator** — called stash — used for fast allocation of fixed-size objects. A stash maintains a free list per size class and a chain of large slabs that those objects are carved out of.

nodes.label: memory-status.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: memory-status.cpp is an **almost-empty placeholder file** that exposes three trivial int-returning functions intended for future memory-statistics reporting. Today they return constant sentinels.

nodes.label: monideal-minprimes.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: monideal-minprimes.cpp implements **MinimalPrimes** — the state machine that computes the **minimal primes** of a MonomialIdeal. It is a specialised cousin of AssociatedPrimes, focused only on the **minimal** primes (smallest codimension); AssociatedPrimes does the full set.

nodes.label: monideal.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: monideal.cpp implements the engine's specialised representation of a **monomial ideal** — an ideal generated by monomials, kept in a form that exploits the combinatorial structure for much faster computations than the general polynomial-ideal path.

nodes.label: monoid.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: Monoid is the engine's representation of the multiplicative side of a polynomial ring: a finite set of named variables together with a monomial ordering and (multi-)grading.

nodes.label: monomial-collection.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: monomial-collection.{cpp,hpp} is the engine's **set-of-monomials** helper class, in transition between two names. The header's TODOs (quoted below) sketch the planned cleanup.

nodes.label: monomial-sets.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: monomial-sets.hpp defines **set / hash-set data structures for monomials**. Each set stores monomials of either a fixed size (passed as a template parameter) or variable size (with a length prefix).

nodes.label: monomial.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: monomial.cpp defines **EngineMonomial** — the engine's opaque single-monomial value type that crosses the engine ↔ interpreter boundary. It is the M2-side Monomial (note capitalisation: an M2-level Monomial is one of these), distinct from the encoded monomial layouts that live inside Monoid (file-monoid.md).

nodes.label: monordering.{hpp}
nodes.summary: monordering.cpp is the **implementation** of the user-facing MonomialOrdering constructors. It is the C++ engine code behind the rawLex…, rawGRevLex…, rawWeights…, rawProductMonomialOrdering C entry points.

nodes.label: monsort.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: monsort.hpp declares a **templated sort routine** for monomial-like data. It is a thin, ring-agnostic wrapper around std::sort that delegates the per-element comparison to a user-supplied Sorter type matching a small duck-typed interface.

nodes.label: montable.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: MonomialTable is the engine's **leading-monomial index** — a data structure that maps each monomial in a Gröbner basis to its owning polynomial, with fast divisibility queries. It is the central reduction-lookup structure in gbA and its peers.

nodes.label: montableZZ.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: MonomialTableZZ is the **ZZ-coefficient analogue** of MonomialTable. It indexes leading monomials of a Gröbner basis over ZZ and answers divisibility queries — including the **coefficient** check that distinguishes the ZZ case from the field case.

nodes.label: mpreal.{h}
nodes.summary: mpreal.h is a **vendored copy of mpreal** by Pavel Holoborodko — an MPFR C++ wrapper that provides operator-overloaded arbitrary-precision real arithmetic on top of MPFR's C API.

nodes.label: mutablecomplex.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: MutableComplex is the engine's representation of a **mutable chain complex** — a sequence of MutableMatrix differentials with in-place editing. It is the cousin of Matrix's mutable variant, generalised to a multi-step complex.

nodes.label: mutablemat-defs.{hpp}
nodes.summary: mutablemat-defs.hpp and its companion mutablemat-imp.hpp are the **template declaration** and **template implementation** halves of MutableMat<Mat> — the templated class behind the abstract MutableMatrix interface.

nodes.label: mutablemat-imp.{hpp}
nodes.summary: mutablemat-imp.hpp contains **template implementations** of MutableMat<Mat> methods that are too long to live inline in mutablemat.hpp. Primarily the **straight-line program (SLP) evaluator** glue for numerical algebraic geometry.

nodes.label: mutablemat.{hpp}
nodes.summary: MutableMatrix is the engine's **mutable** matrix abstraction. Unlike the immutable Matrix, entries can be changed in place, columns swapped, rows reduced.

nodes.label: myalloc.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: myalloc.hpp defines **StatsAllocator** — a tiny instrumented allocator wrapper used during **debugging** and **benchmarking** to count and report allocations of a specific type. It is *not* used in production builds; the class is single-threaded and intentionally trivial.

nodes.label: newdelete.{hpp}
nodes.summary: newdelete.hpp (in subdirectories) declares **our_new_delete** and **our_new_gc** — the two operator new / operator delete overloads that route engine-side allocations through bdwgc, the Boehm-Demers-Weiser garbage collector. Inheriting from these gives a class GC-managed storage at no per-allocation cost beyond the bdwgc allocator's own.

nodes.label: ntl-interface.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: ntl-interface.{cpp,hpp} is the **engine bridge** to Victor Shoup's NTL (Number Theory Library). NTL is linked into M2 for selected operations — integer LLL, integer matrix LLL, factoring, and primality — even though the engine's primary number- theory back end is FLINT.

nodes.label: overflow-test.{cpp}
nodes.summary: overflow-test.cpp is a **standalone microbenchmark** for the engine's safe-integer-arithmetic primitives in overflow.hpp. It's not part of the engine library — it's compiled separately when developers want to measure overflow-check cost.

nodes.label: overflow.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: overflow.cpp provides **checked integer arithmetic** for the small-integer operations the engine performs on monomial exponents and degrees. A silent overflow in a monomial exponent can corrupt a Gröbner basis without any visible error — these helpers ensure that doesn't happen.

nodes.label: pfaff.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: pfaff.cpp computes **Pfaffians** of skew-symmetric matrices. The Pfaffian Pf(A) of a 2n × 2n skew-symmetric matrix A satisfies Pf(A)² = det(A).

nodes.label: points.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: points.cpp declares **PointsComputation<CoeffRing>** — a templated routine for computing the ideal of a finite set of points, given as a matrix of coordinates. The output is a generating set (typically a Gröbner basis under graded reverse lex) plus the standard monomial basis of the quotient.

nodes.label: poly.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: poly.cpp defines **PolyRing** — the engine's standard polynomial ring class. It subclasses PolyRingFlat (a flatness intermediate; "flat" means coefficients live in a non-polynomial base ring) and is the immediate parent of the various flavoured polynomial rings (PolyRingSkew, WeylAlgebra, etc.).

nodes.label: polyquotient.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: polyquotient.cpp defines **PolyQuotient** — the concrete Ring subclass for R/I where R is a PolyRing (or a flavoured variant) and I is a polynomial ideal with a known Gröbner basis. It uses QRingInfo for the bookkeeping state.

nodes.label: polyring.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: PolynomialRing is the engine's polynomial ring R[x_1,…,x_n]. It is the single most heavily reused class in the engine — almost every algorithm in e/ is parameterised by a PolynomialRing*.

nodes.label: qring.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: qring.cpp provides the **bookkeeping for a polynomial-ring quotient** R/I. It is *not* a separate Ring subclass — PolyQuotient (declared in polyring.hpp) is the ring class, while QRingInfo here is the data attached to it.

nodes.label: reader.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: reader.hpp provides a **templated Reader<RingType>** class — reads ring elements from a std::istream. Used for matrix / polynomial I/O, test input, and any path that needs to parse serialised ring elements.

nodes.label: reducedgb.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: After a Gröbner basis is computed, the engine canonicalises it to a **reduced GB**: each leading monomial is unique, no element's tail is divisible by any other element's leading monomial, and (over a field) leading coefficients are 1. This page covers the family of classes that does that pass.

nodes.label: relem.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: RingElement is the engine's representation of an element of a ring, visible to the interpreter as the opaque type behind every polynomial / integer / rational / field-element value the user manipulates.

nodes.label: ring-vecs.{cpp}
nodes.summary: ring-vecs.cpp defines the **Ring class's vector operations** — how a ring's elements assemble into and operate within vecs (the engine's sparse column-of-coefficients value type used to build Matrix columns and FreeModule elements).

nodes.label: ring.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: ring.hpp and ring.cpp define **Ring** — the abstract base class for every coefficient and polynomial ring in M2's older (legacy) ring interface. The whole ring_elem-based API is methods on this class.

nodes.label: ringelem.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: ringelem.hpp is the **single most heavily-included header in the engine**. It declares ring_elem — the universal value type that every ring's elements share at the engine boundary — plus the underlying numeric type aliases.

nodes.label: ringmap.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: RingMap is the engine's representation of a homomorphism R → S between two rings. The map is specified by giving images for each generator of R (as elements of S).

nodes.label: sagbi.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: sagbi.cpp contains **helper routines for computing SAGBI bases** (Subalgebra Analog to Gröbner Bases In). A SAGBI basis for a subalgebra A ⊂ R is a generating set whose leading-term subalgebra generates the leading-term subalgebra of A.

nodes.label: schorder.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: SchreyerOrder is the engine's storage of a **Schreyer order** on a free module. It is a lightweight class that lives on a FreeModule and supplies the data needed to compare two basis elements during resolution code.

nodes.label: schur-poly-heap.{hpp}
nodes.summary: schur-poly-heap.hpp declares **schur_poly_heap** — a geometric heap specialised for accumulating Schur-polynomial sums during LR-style multiplications in file-schur2.md's SchurRing2.

nodes.label: schur.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: schur.cpp implements **SchurRing** — the engine's representation of the ring of **Schur functions**, the basis of symmetric functions indexed by partitions. It is the engine's home for symmetric-function computations such as Littlewood-Richardson coefficients and Schur expansion.

nodes.label: schur2.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: schur2.cpp implements **SchurRing2** — a refactored, more flexible Schur-function ring class that supersedes file-schur.md's SchurRing. The "2" in the name indicates the second-generation implementation; both are in the tree.

nodes.label: schurSn.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: schurSn.cpp implements **SchurSnRing** — the engine's Schur ring specialised for the **representation theory of the symmetric group S_n**. Characters of irreducible S_n representations are indexed by partitions of n; their product (in the sense of the representation ring) is the **Kronecker product**.

nodes.label: skew.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: SkewMultiplication is the **configuration object** for skew-commutative multiplication. It is attached to a PolyRing (and to F4's MonomialInfo) when the user has declared some variables skew.

nodes.label: skewpoly.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: SkewPolynomialRing implements **skew-commutative** polynomial rings — the generalisation of exterior algebras where a designated subset of variables anticommutes (and squares to zero) while the rest commute normally.

nodes.label: smat.{hpp}
nodes.summary: SMat<ACoeffRing> is the engine's **sparse matrix template** — the sister of DMat<R> for matrices where most entries are zero.

nodes.label: solvable.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: SolvableAlgebra implements **PBW-style solvable algebras** — algebras that look like polynomial rings except that the commutation x_j x_i (for i < j) can equal a fixed lower-order polynomial q_{ij} instead of just x_i x_j.

nodes.label: spair.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: spair.cpp defines the **S-pair** data structure used by gbA and several sibling GB algorithms. An S-pair is the unit of work in Buchberger-style algorithms: pick two basis elements, compute the S-polynomial, reduce it.

nodes.label: style.{hpp}
nodes.summary: style.hpp is a tiny **engine-wide stylistic header**. It defines a handful of constants and macros — comparison-result codes, the INTSIZE(x) cast, the GEOHEAP_SIZE constant — that essentially every engine file uses.

nodes.label: text-io.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: text-io.cpp is a thin layer of text-formatting helpers built on top of the engine's buffer class: number formatting, wrapped line emission, indentation-aware writing. The goal is a uniform appearance across all engine-produced text without each caller re-implementing wrap logic.

nodes.label: timing.{hpp}
nodes.summary: timing.hpp declares **engine-side timing helpers** — small wrappers around std::chrono (or equivalent) that engine code uses to record elapsed time. It supplies the timestamps the SLP evaluator (file-SLP-imp.md) reports and that benchmarks across the engine use.

nodes.label: tower.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: tower.cpp implements **Tower** — the engine's **legacy** ring class for iterated finite extensions of Z/p. It pre-dates the aring-based file-aring-tower.md and is still used as a fallback path and by code that hasn't migrated.

nodes.label: util.{hpp}
nodes.summary: util.hpp is a tiny **utility header** with string and array conversion helpers between the engine's M2 types (M2_string, M2_arrayint) and the standard library's std::string, std::vector<int>. Including it costs almost nothing; the few inline functions it declares are usable everywhere.

nodes.label: weylalg.{cpp,hpp}
nodes.summary: WeylAlgebra implements the **Weyl algebra**: the ring of polynomial differential operators. Each "variable" comes in two flavours — a coordinate x_i and its derivative ∂_i = ∂/∂x_i — with the relation ∂_i x_i = x_i ∂_i + 1.

nodes.label: NCAlgebras/
nodes.summary: **See architecture.md** for the standalone architectural reference (three core abstractions FreeMonoid/FreeAlgebra/FreeAlgebraQuotient, the two NC GB algorithms NCGroebner and NCF4, suffix-tree-based overlap detection, memory model).

nodes.label: NCResolutions/
nodes.summary: **See architecture.md** for the standalone architectural reference (current scope, two-line architecture, entry point, why-separate-from-NCAlgebras, algorithmic differences vs commutative, pending future work).

nodes.label: bibasis/
nodes.summary: **See architecture.md** for the standalone architectural reference (Boolean-ring specialisation, 64-bit packed monomial trick, involutive-vs-Gröbner distinction, Janet tree data structure, templated dispatch on monomial order, FastAllocator slab strategy).

nodes.label: doxygen-settings/
nodes.summary: Doxygen configuration overrides and stylesheet customisations for the engine's C++ API documentation. Consumed by the Doxygen run wired into the Sphinx build under Macaulay2/docs/.

nodes.label: f4/
nodes.summary: **See architecture.md** for the standalone architectural reference (pipeline, three-layer design, Macaulay-matrix sweep details, memory model, comparison with gb-f4/).

nodes.label: gb-f4/
nodes.summary: **See architecture.md** for the standalone architectural reference (the newf4:: namespace, typed-integer family, struct-of-arrays polynomial representation, monomial hashing, comparison with original f4/).

nodes.label: interface/
nodes.summary: **See architecture.md** for the standalone architectural reference (the boundary contract, IM2_<Type>_<verb> convention, dispatch pattern, three-layer separation, file-by-file roles, "how to add a new public function").

nodes.label: schreyer-resolution/
nodes.summary: **See architecture.md** for the standalone architectural reference (Schreyer-frame trick, three-layer design, TBB task-graph parallelism, dense vs sparse monoid choice, memory model).

nodes.label: unit-tests/
nodes.summary: **See architecture.md** for the standalone architectural reference (four-layer design: harness → fixtures → helpers → per-area tests; test patterns including templated cross-backend validation; floating-point almostEqual helpers; build wiring; why test the engine in C++ directly).
